fileops.py:670 calls existing_or_409 inside physical_delete. purge_all_trash (756-759) commits only after the loop. Earlier files are unlinked at line 673, and their rows are deleted in the session. When a later file raises 409, nothing is committed, so rows remain for files already gone from disk. purge_all_missing commits per batch of 200, so it only affects the current batch. The Missing rows self-heal on the next scan, but the trash rows are left pointing at deleted files. The 409 is new with this change.

upload.py:247-248 resolves the parent strictly with new_or_409, then resolves the leaf with non-strict resolve_on_disk. An NFD twin created after init_upload is therefore replaced in place. This matches the I7 'in-place replacement' answer for a same-spelling collision. It needs a race between init and complete, so impact is small under the single-user threat model.
